subject: Final-mile lifeboat: procurement cordoning & MAP retarget
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike@heliumhealth.com>, Helium Health Procurement <procurement@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final-mile lifeboat: procurement cordoning & MAP retarget

Mike / Procurement team —

Quick update from our side on the mutual action plan (MAP) and a request to cordon the procurement lane to avoid a full close derail. We saw the PO timeline slip this morning (internal notes: procurement paperwork queued for security review) which pushes the expected PO receipt out by ~2 weeks.

What we need from you to prevent a broader go/no-go:
- Confirm whether the PO can land by Oct 20 (our internal go-live window needs a signed PO + SOW)
- If PO timing is uncertain, can procurement accept a 30% invoice credit for month 1 while you complete internal approvals (we can invoice on ship with credit applied once PO arrives)?
- Sign the attached MAP v3 (helium_map_v3.pdf) with the updated evaluation milestones — we re-baselined the canary & acceptance gates to preserve the cutover date if procurement finalizes within the next 3 weeks.

We will hold the canary deployment in a soft-lock rather than cancel; that avoids full rollback work and keeps the cutover runway intact. If procurement cannot commit to Oct 20, we will need to formally re-baseline the MAP and trigger our escalation ladder (see section at bottom).

Proposed next steps: 30 min sync tomorrow to confirm PO path and any security evidence they need. I copied Jordan and Marissa to coordinate procurement cordoning and any SLA exception forms.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Attachments: helium_map_v3.pdf

Thanks, Irene — appreciate the heads-up.

Short version: procurement cycle extended due to an unexpected platform security questionnaire and a backlog in our finance PO queue. Realistically the earliest procurement can get a signed PO to you is Oct 25–27 unless we get an internal exception.

I can escalate to CFO for a short-lane approval but will need a formal ask from Redwood (SLA exception, proposed credit, and the exact DocuSign URL). Attaching a short note from procurement on outstanding items (procurement_response_q3.docx).

If you can offer a temporary credit on month 1 and keep the canary in soft-lock, that makes a lot of sense. Also: we need a clear list of evidence artifacts for security (SOC2 scope statement + data-retention note).

On the sync: can we do 11:00 PT Monday?

—Mike
Mike Chen
Director of Engineering, Helium Health

Marissa / Kim —

Forwarding Helium's note. TL;DR: procurement now says PO may slip to Oct 25–27. I propose we offer a limited lifeboat to preserve the close:

1) Soft-lock canary (no rollback; hold incremental deploy)
2) Offer 30% credit on month 1 invoice if PO not in hand by Oct 20; credit applied retroactively upon PO receipt
3) Request immediate completion of DocuSign (Irene please send final link) for legal/SOW signature to remove signature gating
4) Prepare SLA exception form to send to procurement + execs (attached draft: redwood_sla_exception_form.pdf)
5) Trigger: if PO not received by EOD Oct 27 then we auto-rebaseline the MAP and move cutover out by 2 weeks — notify execs and start rollback contingency window.

Can you and Marissa own the cordoning comms? I will handle the credit approval path with finance (we'll mark as temporary, reversible). If agreed I'll propose the 11:00 PT Monday sync and draft a one-page executive note for CFO.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Final-mile lifeboat: procurement cordoning & MAP retarget — escalation note + re-baseline proposal

Team / Mike —

Agree with Jordan's salvage playbook. Adding the formal escalation note for visibility to sales leadership and a compact re-baseline proposal to avoid ambiguity:

- Escalation note: If PO not received by Oct 27 EOD, Sales will open a formal escalation to CRO and CS VP. We will mark the deal in HubSpot as "Procurement Hold — Escalation Enabled" and schedule an exec readout.
- Re-baseline proposal: Move acceptance gate + final cutover by +14 calendar days (new cutover target Oct 28 -> Nov 11). During the +14 day window we will keep canary soft-locked and prioritize the Helium environment for capacity.
- Rollback trigger: If PO not signed by Nov 11 then automatic cutover cancellation and refund/credit settlement commences per commercial terms.

Marissa attaches a mini risk register for this thread (inline):
1) Risk: Procurement PO slip beyond Oct 27 -> Impact: Project cutover delayed by 2+ weeks -> Mitigation: Temporary credit + exec escalation
2) Risk: Security evidence lag (SOC2 artifact) -> Impact: Procurement refuses to sign -> Mitigation: Deliver scoped evidence package + security kickoff meeting; Kim owns delivery
3) Risk: Finance hold on credit -> Impact: inability to offer lifeboat -> Mitigation: Jordan to secure provisional sign-off from Finance Controller

Next steps:
- Irene: send DocuSign link + final MAP v3 sign-off copy to procurement (cc Linda from DocuSign)
- Kim: collate SOC2 scoped notes and timeline to send by Monday EOD
- Jordan: confirm provisional finance approval and prep exec one-pager

I'll update HubSpot with the re-baseline plan and flag deal HLTH-4821 for leadership watch.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Final-mile lifeboat: procurement cordoning & MAP retarget — decision record

Mike / Procurement team —

Thanks for the sync today. Quick decision record and asks so we have a single-source-of-truth: 

Decisions made:
- Redwood will cordon procurement lane and hold the canary in a soft-lock to avoid rollback work.
- Redwood will provide a 30% credit on month 1 invoice if PO is not in-hand by Oct 20; credit applied retroactively upon PO receipt.
- If PO not fully signed by Oct 27 EOD, we will re-baseline MAP (cutover -> Nov 11) and trigger the escalation ladder.

Immediate asks from Helium Health:
1) Finalize DocuSign by close of business Wed, Oct 7 -> Linda: please confirm the DocuSign URL is active (link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-hel-health).
2) Procurement: confirm PO target date (Oct 20 preferred; latest acceptable Oct 27). Please reply to procurement@heliumhealth.com and cc this thread.
3) Security: confirm which SOC2 artifacts are required; Kim, please include the list by Monday EOD so Helium can route to the security reviewer.

Attached: updated MAP v3 (helium_map_v3.pdf) with the re-baseline table and the SLA exception form we discussed (redwood_sla_exception_form.pdf). I will update HubSpot (HLTH-4821) with this decision record and add the exec watch flag.

If Procurement can meet Oct 20 we will keep original cutover. If not, expect the Nov 11 re-baseline to be published on Oct 28.

Thanks again for working through this — we want to avoid churn and keep the project economically intact for both teams.
